memory_update.text: MU is the cleanest US-listed direct HBM mapping in this node; verify HBM revenue, customer commitments, and HBM4/HBM4E ramp status in the next earnings call.
AMKR should be tracked as a US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity candidate, but the research layer must separate broad packaging exposure from true AI/HBM advanced-packaging utilization.

ONTO and CAMT are high-relevance inspection/metrology beneficiaries for HBM and advanced packaging; both have explicit HBM/AI packaging disclosures and should be compared on tool share, customer concentration, and backlog conversion.
ACMR is a less obvious advanced-packaging equipment candidate with global customer orders, but its HBM-specific linkage is an inference and needs tool-of-record/customer validation.

Non-US-listed but important node controllers remain outside this pass: SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, TSMC, ASE, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Kinsus, Disco, Besi, and ASMPT. Later layers should map US ADR/accessibility and supplier dependencies.
The expanded US-listed universe for this node clusters into: HBM capacity controller, OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity, inspection/metrology, and wafer/panel-level advanced-packaging equipment.

node: HBM, advanced memory, and advanced packaging
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the AI HBM / advanced-packaging chokepoint. The strongest direct mappings are Micron as a US-listed HBM producer, Amkor as an OSAT/advanced-packaging provider, and Onto/Camtek as inspection and metrology vendors tied to HBM, micro-bumps, 2.5D/3D packaging, and heterogeneous integration. ACM Research is included as a less obvious second-order beneficiary because it has announced advanced-packaging tool orders across wafer-level and panel-level packaging; its direct HBM exposure still needs customer-level validation.
